phaseName: Phase 8, the light look: the page, the cards and both decks in Elisa's colours, video v6 on the same voice; package V5 on the Desktop; the hosted copy on Cloudflare Containers for the jury; the owner's upload, submission and vote remain
state: Session 2 (6.11.2026, Code on the Mac): Elisa's challenge is selected and the decisions P1 to P6 are made. Phase 0 (skeleton, health check), phase 1 (Elisa's files unchanged, synthetic sources, events, seed graph, truth set, held-out binding set) phase 2 (store, export, /graph), phase 3 (extraction, binding, merging, recorded answers, scoring) phase 4 (claims_for, access_for, the prohibition, counters from telemetry), phase 5 (firmware recheck, outcomes from telemetry, the log line from device events) and phase 6 (the page, ten scenes) are in main. Session 3 (7.11.2026, Code on the Mac): a technical check, then the owner's checkpoint: the page looked confusing at first glance, so it was rebuilt for clarity (a story per scene, plain words, readable evidence, named claims) and waits for a second look. The product is named Silent context and the repository is renamed. The Cypher export loads into Neo4j. A clean install from git archive passed with no key. Phase 7 is done: docs/acceptance.md holds the build plan's cases A0 to A11 and a test keeps every computed row passing. The README has its diagram and its tested section, and docs/what-is-simulated.md exists. Phase 8: the owner approved the larger-text picture as a pre-version on 7.11. and asked for two things, both built: the captions in a black band under the picture (never over it) and a 20 second pitch in front (two cards in the page's look, narration blocks 01 and 02). The MCP wrapper (app/mcp_server.py, the mcp package) exposes claims_for, access_for and source as tools, tested over an in-memory transport and as a real stdio process. The owner voiced the narration in ElevenLabs, and the final video is built: 127.2 s, 1920 by 1080, the captions in the band, in the pipeline's media folder and in the owner's Desktop folder. The repository went public under the MIT licence on 7.11. after gitleaks found nothing in the full history. The slides exist: docs/slides/silent-context.pptx and the PDF beside it, ten slides from docs/slides.md in the page's look, with speaker notes, every sentence read against the README, acceptance.md and what-is-simulated.md, rendered and looked at; written by the scripts in docs/slides/build/. Session 4 (7.11.2026, Code on the Mac): the builders' guide was read: the video is accepted only as a public or unlisted YouTube link, no file; the form's fields are known and every field's text is in the Desktop folder's submission-notes.md (a 128-character tagline, the About text, Built with, the GenAI answer); the PDF goes in as the pitch deck. The work was read as a judge and as an ordinary viewer (README, narration, the ten scenes, the slide text): nothing changed in the product, the findings are in the CHANGELOG. Sunday: the deadline 10:00, the participant vote 10:00 to 12:00, finalists at 12:00, presence needed only from finalists. Later in session 4: the README's Demo section opens with a picture of the page at scene 4; the owner has a Finnish plain-language paper on the Desktop ("Silent context suomeksi", not in the repository); a second cut of the video on a plain-language narration v3 is proposed as decision 18 (A new cut, B zooms and story cards on the existing take, C keep), open. The owner chose A for decision 18 and the second cut was built the same evening: narration v3 in plain words, four story cards, the page zoomed toward the panel each sentence is about, the owner's new ElevenLabs track aligned to it; the final is 117.6 s, 12.7 MB, in the Desktop folder "Silent context submission" beside the first cut. The submission package is now the Desktop folder "Silent context submission V2": the second cut, the five-picture deck (docs/slides/silent-context-in-five.pdf, from docs/slides/five/) as the pitch deck, the full deck as a supporting document, the zip and the notes; the first package stays in "Silent context submission" as the fallback. After the owner watched the second cut, the v4 words add a pause on the whole view after the pitch; the cards are timed from the aligned voice and every zoom follows a second of the whole view; in the page block each part lights up as the voice names it and the close card names the MCP tools; the final is 135.4 s, 15.1 MB (a one-frame flash of the opening card before the limits card found and fixed), in the Desktop folder "Silent context submission V3" with the five-picture deck, the full deck, the notes and the zip. V2 and the first folder are fallbacks. Later on 7.11. (decision 19, A): a policy on who acts (app/policy.py), a fourth unit TRN-063 and the agent's own bounce in the synthetic stream, a Teams thread in Finnish and a ticket export as sources, the question drafted with a budget when the agent does not know; the page has thirteen scenes; video v5 is 176.5 s on the owner's voice; the five-picture deck and the twelve-slide deck follow; 160 tests, the truth set 13/13 found, 9/9 merged, 8/8 evidence, the held-out set 1 of 16. The package is the Desktop folder "Silent context submission V4". Session 4 closed 7.11. at about 17:50: the owner's word that package V4 is the submit version, open to further work if something comes up; the form opens 18:00 EET. Session 5 (7.11.2026, late evening, Code on the Mac): the owner's read of the whole after V4: the look was never decided and the result was very dark, and a live demo for the form's optional Demo URL field (judges see it, voters do not; the builders' guide: "A link where your project can be tried, if it is deployed"). Decision 24: a light look with elements of Elisa's own, measured from elisa.fi's stylesheets (blue 600 #005fed, orange #ff6400, its greys, navy text, Jost for headings). One token block in web/style.css; the story cards, the five-picture deck and the deck script take the same values; the page loads nothing from outside (the Google Fonts link was tried and the test caught it, so Jost is served from web/fonts under its OFL licence, on the owner's word the same evening). The five-picture deck's crops end at an element's edge now, so no sentence is cut, and its first page is centred. Both decks rebuilt (the PDF with LibreOffice and Office's fonts), the README's picture re-shot. Video v6: a new take of the v5 words on the aligned v5 voice, the light look, nothing in the narration or alignment changed. Package V5 on the Desktop. The hosted demo (Cloudflare Containers, Workers Paid on the account) is proposed as a side session with its brief; its address goes into the Demo URL field and the README's Demo section. 160 tests pass. The hosting side session (7.11. evening, Code on the Mac): the app as it is in a Docker image on Cloudflare Containers behind a small Worker, one instance of the basic type, at https://silent-context.pkorrrhonen.workers.dev; published with one command from hosting/ (docs/hosting.md), twice, the second time after the font commit. The demo clock and the agent's log there are shared by whoever is on the page, and the README's Demo section says so; a cron keeps the instance awake on Sundays 08:00 to 13:55 Finnish time, around the jury's hours. Measured: a cold start of 10 s, warm requests 0.15 s, a clock move under half a second. The owner watched v6 and saw two jerks in the zoom and a grey time axis under the dating sentence: the take's frame list showed stalls of 0.3 to 0.4 s inside the first two moves, in the minute other jobs ran beside the recorder, and none in the v5 and v4 takes; the axis was dimmed by the page in that scene. Block 05 now lights the axis for that sentence, the take was recorded again on a quiet machine (55 or 56 frames in every move, no stall), cut and finished; the V5 folder holds the new video and SRT, the notes carry the hosted demo's address, and the zip is rebuilt from main's tip after the hosting commit.

next_session.scope: Everything the submission needs is built and in the Desktop folder "Silent context submission V5" (video v6 on the light look, the five-picture deck, the full deck, the zip from main's tip, submission-notes.md with every field's text; the Demo URL is https://silent-context.pkorrrhonen.workers.dev, redeployed with one command from hosting/ after any change to app/, web/ or data/, as docs/hosting.md says). What remains is the owner's: the YouTube upload as unlisted (P-10), the submission in sinceai.app from Saturday 18:00 EET, by Sunday 09:30 at the latest (P-3), and the vote Sunday 10:00 to 12:00 (P-11). The look is one token block in web/style.css, mirrored in video/story.html, docs/slides/five/five.html and docs/slides/build/deck.js. A change to the words is a change to video/narration-v5.md and a new ElevenLabs track, aligned first; a change to the picture is video/story.html or video/scenes_story.py and a new take with SILENT_CONTEXT_ALIGNMENT set, then cut_from_take.py, assemble and final as video/README.md says; the zip is rebuilt after every commit to main. Rule authors do not read data/truth/decoys, expected_decoys.json or data/extractions/decoys. After the event: REPO-2 (the Atlas system, then docs/adr/), P-8 (the main PC's remote), DOC-2 (architecture.md).
next_session.gate: The owner's submission in sinceai.app, from Saturday 18:00 EET and by Sunday 8.11. 09:30, the v6 video as an unlisted YouTube link, the hosted demo's address in the Demo URL field.

workflow: Code, comments, commits and documentation in English; conversation with the owner in Finnish. During the event straight to main in small commits; never force-push or rewrite history. One phase at a time, a line to the Atlas thread at each phase's end, the owner's checkpoint after phases 1, 3, 4 and 6. End a session by updating BUILD_INFO.json, CHANGELOG.md, BACKLOG.md, DECISIONS.md and, when a lesson was paid for, LESSONS.md.
